subject: Reusable UI component-library architecture

cases.scenario: A product designer asks how a dashboard page should arrange analytics, alerts, filters, and recent activity modules into named regions.
cases.context: The components already exist; the question is about a single product's page composition.
cases.question: Should component-architecture own this request?
expected_flags: This is design-module-composition, not component-library architecture.
The task is within-product module wiring and layout regions.
Component architecture may matter only if existing components cannot support the assembly.
expected_fix_hints: Escalate back only if reusable component APIs need redesign.
absent_signals: Do not redesign the component library when the issue is page/module arrangement.
Do not treat one product page layout as a reusable component layer.

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: This is design-module-composition, not component-library architecture.
Surfaces this expected flag: The task is within-product module wiring and layout regions.
Surfaces this expected flag: Component architecture may matter only if existing components cannot support the assembly.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Route to design-module-composition.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Escalate back only if reusable component APIs need redesign.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not redesign the component library when the issue is page/module arrangement.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not treat one product page layout as a reusable component layer.

cases.scenario: A team needs a Dialog component that works in three products: one uses brand-heavy marketing styling, one uses dense admin UI, and one uses mobile-first interaction. The current Dialog has 26 style and behavior props.
cases.context: The component must keep focus management and keyboard behavior stable while allowing product-specific visual treatment.
cases.question: How should the agent redesign the component architecture?
expected_flags: Classifies Dialog behavior as primitive/headless responsibility.
Separates headless behavior from styled wrappers or token-bound presentation.
Uses compound parts such as Root, Trigger, Content, Title, Description, and Close when structure varies.
Avoids prop explosion for open-ended visual and structural variation.
Documents API contract, accessibility requirements, and migration/deprecation path.
Keeps product-specific assemblies outside the primitive.
expected_fix_hints: Use slots or compound components for structure.
Expose controlled/uncontrolled open state if both consumer types exist.
Bind styled layer to tokens rather than hardcoded brand values.
absent_signals: Do not add another set of product-specific props to the primitive.
Do not let a product assembly import back into the primitive.
Do not split out styling by losing keyboard/focus accessibility behavior.

cases.scenario: A reusable Select component keeps value internally, but one product needs URL-synchronized state, another needs form-library control, and a third wants a simple default value.
cases.context: The team asks whether to make three Select variants.
cases.question: What state contract should the component expose?
expected_flags: Identifies state contract as component architecture, not app-wide state management.
Recommends a hybrid controlled/uncontrolled API when both consumer kinds are real.
Uses `value`/`onChange` for controlled consumers and `defaultValue` for uncontrolled consumers.
Keeps event semantics stable and documented.
Avoids separate variants that duplicate primitive behavior.
expected_fix_hints: Ensure form and URL consumers can own state without forking the component.
Preserve accessibility and keyboard behavior in the primitive layer.
absent_signals: Do not force all consumers into internal component state.
Do not route this to state-management unless the question is app-level ownership.
Do not hide value changes behind imperative-only refs.

cases.scenario: A component library hardcodes colors, spacing, and icons inside behavior primitives. A second product wants the same interactions with a different brand language.
cases.context: The first product works, but reuse is failing.
cases.question: How should the agent repair the layer structure?
expected_flags: Flags visual language hardcoded into reusable behavior.
Separates headless behavior from styled/token-bound wrappers.
Keeps accessibility, focus, keyboard behavior, and ARIA in the primitive layer.
Moves brand treatment to styled components, tokens, or product assemblies.
Explains dependency direction and prevents primitives from importing product-specific assets.
expected_fix_hints: Introduce primitive/headless parts if interaction behavior is reusable.
Create styled wrappers per product or theme.
Verify with at least two real consumers or themes.
absent_signals: Do not duplicate the entire behavior implementation for each brand.
Do not make token selection itself the component-architecture task.
Do not remove accessibility behavior while extracting styles.

cases.scenario: A Card component has independent props for header variants, footer actions, media layouts, badge placement, loading state, and product-specific CTA logic.
cases.context: New variants keep multiplying and consumers cannot predict combinations.
cases.question: How should the agent choose between configuration and composition?
expected_flags: Recognizes independent prop multiplication as a configuration-explosion smell.
Keeps small closed enum variations as props only when combinations are limited.
Uses children, named slots, or compound components for open structural variation.
Moves product-specific CTA logic into product assemblies or callbacks.
Documents the public API and migration path.
expected_fix_hints: Split primitive visual frame from composed sections.
Use Card.Root, Card.Header, Card.Media, Card.Body, Card.Footer, or equivalent slots.
Preserve backwards compatibility through deprecation where needed.
absent_signals: Do not add more boolean props for every new layout.
Do not make the component know every product CTA.
Do not collapse all variation into an untyped `config` object.

cases.scenario: A design team asks for semantic color roles, contrast ramps, theme palettes, and token names for a new component library.
cases.context: They are not asking how components consume the tokens.
cases.question: Should component-architecture own this request?
expected_flags: This is color-system-design or visual-design-foundations.
Component architecture consumes tokens but does not choose the palette or contrast strategy.
The boundary is visual language versus structural component API.
expected_fix_hints: Route palette and token semantics to color-system-design.
Return to component architecture when binding tokens to reusable component layers.
absent_signals: Do not decide the color system inside the component API task.
Do not hardcode selected colors into reusable behavior primitives.

Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not hardcode selected colors into reusable behavior primitives.

cases.scenario: A team asks how checkout validation errors should appear, when to validate fields, how to group fields, and how the submit flow should recover from server errors.
cases.context: The question is about form behavior and user experience, not the reusable API of Input or FormField primitives.
cases.question: Should component-architecture own this request?
expected_flags: This is form-ux-architecture.
Component architecture owns reusable FormField/Input contracts, not form-specific validation and submission flow.
The component skill can verify that components support the form UX without owning the form strategy.
expected_fix_hints: Route form validation and submit UX to form-ux-architecture.
Use component architecture only for reusable field primitives and state contracts.
absent_signals: Do not solve form validation strategy by adding ad hoc props to Input.
Do not confuse component state contract with full form state architecture.
